# Test fixture corpus

This directory holds the PDF files used by this module's tests. Keeping
their provenance and license status written down here is a Phase 0 exit
criterion (see the "Phased Plan" section of the repository README): a
test corpus is only trustworthy if every file in it can be redistributed
and its origin is clear.

## handmade/

Every file under `handmade/` is generated by
[`tools/genfixtures`](../../tools/genfixtures/main.go), a small Go program
that is part of this repository. The PDF *content* of each fixture (the
object structure, page tree shape, and any deliberate corruption) was
authored specifically for this project's tests; the generator only
handles the mechanical, error-prone parts of PDF authoring — mainly
computing byte-exact cross-reference offsets — so that regenerating the
corpus is reproducible instead of relying on hand-maintained byte
offsets.

**License:** these files are original work of this project and are
covered by the repository's own [LICENSE](../../LICENSE) (MIT), the same
as the Go source code that generates them.

**Do not hand-edit the `.pdf` files in this directory.** Any manual edit
desynchronizes their cross-reference table from the file's actual byte
layout, producing a fixture that is broken for reasons unrelated to
whatever it was meant to test. Instead, edit
[`tools/genfixtures/main.go`](../../tools/genfixtures/main.go) and
regenerate with:

```sh
go run ./tools/genfixtures
```

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `minimal-blank-page.pdf` | Simplest valid PDF this project should be able to open: one page, no drawn content, a classic (table-based) cross-reference table, single trailer. |
| `two-pages.pdf` | Two pages under one Pages node with distinct MediaBox sizes, to test page-tree (`Kids`/`Count`) traversal and that per-page attributes aren't shared or swapped between pages. |
| `incremental-update.pdf` | A file that has been incrementally saved once: the original single-page revision is followed by an appended update that adds a second page and rewrites the Pages object, with a second trailer chained to the first via `/Prev`. Regression fixture for readers that only look at the final trailer and ignore earlier revisions. |
| `malformed-bad-xref-offset.pdf` | Otherwise-valid file with one cross-reference entry deliberately pointed at the wrong byte offset. Exercises malformed-input error classification (and, ideally, recovery via a linear "N G obj" scan). |
| `truncated.pdf` | A valid file cut off partway through, before its cross-reference table and trailer exist at all. Simulates a partial download or interrupted write. |
| `xref-stream.pdf` | Same page tree as `minimal-blank-page.pdf`, but described by a PDF 1.5+ cross-reference *stream* (Flate-compressed, non-default `/W` field widths) instead of a classic table. |
| `object-stream.pdf` | The Pages and Page dictionaries are packed together inside a single object stream (`/Type /ObjStm`), described via type-2 ("compressed") entries in a cross-reference stream; the catalog and content stream remain ordinary top-level objects, matching how real PDF 1.5+ producers mix both storage forms. |
| `filled-rect.pdf` | One 100x100-point page whose (plain-text) content stream fills an 80x80 red square with a 10-point margin - the baseline Phase 2 rendering fixture (solid color, axis-aligned path, nonzero fill). |
| `stroked-line.pdf` | One 100x100-point page whose content stream strokes a diagonal blue line, corner to corner, with a 5-point line width - exercises stroking with a non-default width. |
| `clipped-rect.pdf` | One 100x100-point page whose content stream clips to a 40x40 centered square, then fills the entire page green - only the clipped square should render green. |
| `transformed-rect.pdf` | One 100x100-point page whose content stream translates to the page center and rotates 45 degrees before filling a square - exercises the current transformation matrix (`cm`) and its `q`/`Q` scoping. |
| `flate-content-rect.pdf` | Identical in appearance to `filled-rect.pdf`, but its content stream is Flate-compressed rather than plain text - exercises filter decoding applied to a page *content* stream specifically (as opposed to `xref-stream.pdf`/`object-stream.pdf`'s use of Flate for structural data). |
| `image-rgb.pdf` | One 100x100-point page whose content stream paints a referenced 2x2 DeviceRGB image XObject (red/green/blue/yellow, one color per quadrant) across the whole page - the baseline Phase 3 referenced-image fixture (`/Resources /XObject` lookup, image dictionary resolution, uncompressed DeviceRGB sample decoding). |
| `image-mask.pdf` | One 100x100-point page that sets the fill color to red, then paints a referenced 2x1 `/ImageMask` stencil image (left pixel painted, right pixel masked out) across the whole page - exercises image masks painting with the current fill color. |
| `image-smask.pdf` | One 100x100-point page that paints a referenced 1x1 solid-red image XObject with a `/SMask` giving it 50% alpha, across the whole page - exercises resolving and decoding a second image object referenced from within the first one's own dictionary, and per-pixel alpha blending against the page's background. |
| `image-jpeg.pdf` | One 100x100-point page that paints a referenced image XObject encoded with `/Filter /DCTDecode`: a solid dark-blue 4x4 JPEG, generated at fixture-build time with the standard library's own `image/jpeg` encoder (quality 100) rather than sourced externally - exercises `internal/filter`'s DCTDecode support through the real cross-reference/object-resolution pipeline. Note: unlike every other fixture, this one's exact bytes depend on Go's `image/jpeg` encoder's output, which is deterministic for a given Go release but is not itself part of this project's own reproducibility guarantee the way the rest of `tools/genfixtures` is - if `TestGeneratedFixturesMatchCheckedInFiles` ever fails only for this file after a Go upgrade, regenerate and re-commit it rather than treating that as a correctness regression. |
| `inline-image.pdf` | One 100x100-point page whose content stream paints an inline (`BI`/`ID`/`EI`) 2x1 DeviceRGB image (red, green), with no `/Resources /XObject` entry at all - exercises `internal/content`'s inline-image parsing end to end, including its computed-exact-length read path (no `/Filter`, so the raw byte count is computed from `/W`, `/H`, `/BPC`, and `/CS` rather than requiring a non-standard `/L` key or a scan for `EI`). |
| `rotated-page.pdf` | A 100 (wide) x 200 (tall) point page declaring `/Rotate 90`, with a 20x20-point red square filled at the origin of its own (unrotated) user space - the Phase 3 regression fixture for `Page.Render`'s and `Page.Thumbnail`'s `/Rotate` handling, which previously had no end-to-end rendering test. See `buildRotatedPage`'s doc comment in `tools/genfixtures/main.go` for the hand-worked-out expected pixel result. |
| `text-simple-truetype.pdf` | One 100x100-point page showing "A" at font size 100 in a simple (`/Subtype /TrueType`) font with an embedded, hand-built minimal TrueType program (a single square glyph, see `tools/genfixtures/truetype.go`) - the baseline Phase 4 rendering fixture. See `buildTextSimpleTrueType`'s doc comment for the hand-derived expected device-space bounding box. |
| `text-scaled.pdf` | One 200x100-point page showing two 'A's with the same embedded font at two different sizes (`Tf` changed mid text object) and repositioned with `Td` between them - exercises font-size scaling and text-position tracking together. See `buildTextScaled`'s doc comment for both glyphs' hand-derived bounding boxes. |
| `text-type0-identity.pdf` | Structurally identical in appearance to `text-simple-truetype.pdf`, but reaches the same embedded glyph through a composite (`/Subtype /Type0`, `/Encoding /Identity-H`) font showing CID 1 instead of a simple font's character code - exercises the entirely separate `internal/fonts/cid.go` code path (`/DescendantFonts`, `/W`, `/CIDToGIDMap /Identity`) and should render pixel-for-pixel identically. |
| `text-notdef-fallback.pdf` | One 100x100-point page showing "A" in a simple font declaring `/BaseFont /Helvetica` with no `/FontFile*` entry at all - exercises this project's missing-glyph fallback (`internal/fonts`' `notdefGlyph`, a hollow placeholder box) rather than a system font lookup this project deliberately never performs. See `buildTextNotdefFallback`'s doc comment for the hand-derived outer/inner box geometry. |
| `text-rotated-page.pdf` | Structurally like `rotated-page.pdf` (a 100x200 `/MediaBox` with `/Rotate 90`), but showing embedded-font text instead of a filled rectangle - Phase 4's end-to-end confirmation that text painting composes correctly with page rotation. See `buildTextRotatedPage`'s doc comment for the by-hand rotated coordinate derivation. |
| `separation-fill.pdf` | One 100x100-point page declaring a named `/Separation` color space (`/CS0`, over `/DeviceRGB`, an inline Type 2 tint-transform function mapping tint 0 to white and tint 1 to a distinctive blue-ish tone) and filling an 80x80 square at tint 1 via `cs`/`scn` - the baseline Phase 5 fixture for a resolved, non-Device color space used directly as a fill color (as opposed to only as an image's `/ColorSpace`, already supported before Phase 5). |
| `lab-fill.pdf` | One 100x100-point page declaring a named `/Lab` color space (`/CS0`, default white point and `a*`/`b*` range) and filling a left/right 50x100 split at `L*=0` (black) and `L*=100` (white) via `cs`/`scn` - the two CIELAB points every plausible conversion must agree on exactly, making this a robust end-to-end check of Phase 5's `/Lab` support. |
| `axial-shading.pdf` | One 100x100-point page whose content stream clips to the whole page and paints a named axial (`/ShadingType 2`) shading directly via `sh`: a black-to-white gradient along the x-axis, via a Type 2 (exponential interpolation) function - the baseline Phase 5 fixture for gradient shadings and the `sh` operator. |
| `radial-shading.pdf` | One 100x100-point page whose content stream paints a named radial (`/ShadingType 3`) shading, unclipped, via `sh`: black at the page's center growing to blue at a radius-50 circle, with `/Extend [false true]` carrying the blue edge color out to the page's corners (which lie outside that circle) - exercises the two-circle radial gradient formula and `/Extend`. |
| `shading-pattern-fill.pdf` | One 100x100-point page whose content stream selects a shading pattern (`/PatternType 2`, wrapping the same black-to-white axial gradient) via `cs Pattern`/`scn`, then fills an 80x80 square with it - exercises a shading used as an ordinary fill paint source (bounded to the filled shape) rather than `sh`'s whole-clip painting, and that the pattern's own coordinate system is independent of the CTM active when it is selected or used. |

## real-world/

Empty for now. Phase 0 permits adding real-world PDF fixtures alongside
the hand-authored ones, but only with their license and source recorded
in a table here at the time they are added — do not add a real-world PDF
fixture without doing so in the same change.

## Rendered reference images

`testdata/renderrefs/` (a sibling of `testdata/fixtures/`, outside this
directory) holds checked-in PNG reference images for Phase 2's rendering
tests — see `pdfviewer_render_test.go`'s `TestRenderMatchesReferenceImages`
in the repository root for the comparison tolerance and how to regenerate
them (`go test . -run TestRenderMatchesReferenceImages -update`) after a
deliberate, reviewed change to rendering output. Same license and
provenance as everything under `handmade/` above: original work of this
project, MIT.
